full_narrative: Student SLIIT_01986: Psychosocial Risk Index is MODERATE (43.2/100). The primary contributing indicator elevating psychosocial risk is moderate levels of situational stress (score: 3.7). This profile is actively buffered by strong intrinsic academic motivation (score: 4.0), moderate sense of campus belongingness (score: 3.5), and moderate academic self-efficacy and belief in capability (score: 3.3). Note that these psychosocial factors serve as contributing indicators to support proactive retention, rather than deterministic causes.
recommendations: Offer time-management workshops, workload review, or academic counseling check-in.
disclaimer: RESEARCH NOTICE: The Psychosocial Risk Index (PRI) is an academic decision-support indicator developed for educational research at SLIIT Kandy. It is not a clinical psychological evaluation or psychiatric diagnosis.
